nodes.label: Improving Transformer Models by Reordering their Sublayers
nodes.author: Ofir Press, Noah A. Smith, Omer Levy

nodes.label: Sandwich Transformer
nodes.rationale: Novel transformer architecture with k self-attention sublayers at bottom, k feedforward at top, and interleaved pattern in middle. Improves language modeling perplexity without additional parameters.

nodes.label: Random Transformer Sublayer Search
nodes.rationale: Empirical exploration of transformer architecture space by randomly permuting self-attention and feedforward sublayers to identify patterns correlating with performance.

nodes.label: WikiText-103 Language Modeling Benchmark
nodes.rationale: Standard benchmark with ~103M tokens from English Wikipedia used to evaluate transformer variants; baseline achieves 18.65±0.24 perplexity.

nodes.label: Attention Distance Metric
nodes.rationale: Measures divergence in attention patterns between models using Hungarian algorithm and earth mover's distance; shows sandwich transformers learn different attention functions than interleaved models.

edges.rationale: Sandwich transformer design is motivated by and derived from random search experiments showing self-attention-first, feedforward-last patterns perform better.
Random search experiments are conducted on WikiText-103 benchmark to identify architectural patterns.
Sandwich transformer is evaluated on WikiText-103, achieving 17.96 perplexity vs 18.63±0.26 baseline.
Attention distance analysis reveals that sandwich transformers learn qualitatively different attention patterns than interleaved models.

hyperedges.label: Transformer Architecture Analysis and Optimization
hyperedges.rationale: These three concepts form a coherent research narrative: random search identifies architectural patterns, sandwich transformer implements the pattern, and attention distance analysis explains the mechanism.
